Adult traumatic hemorrhage uses the AM-05 perfusion-directed warmed isotonic crystalloid strategy when blood is unavailable; the suspected-TBI adult SBP target is at least 110 mmHg. Medical director adopted Medical Control-directed pediatric traumatic-hemorrhage fluid orders for this release on October 31, 2026; no numeric pediatric standing order is established.

Trauma TXA is Paramedic-only after immediate lifesaving interventions for traumatic hemorrhage with clinical hemorrhagic shock within 3 hours. Adult dose/rate accepted October 30, 2026: 1 g IV/IO over 10 minutes or 2 g IV/IO over 20 minutes, maximum 100 mg/min. No automatic repeat dose is provided. Verify stocked concentration/dilution using existing preparation instructions. Pediatric 15 mg/kg is the retained local reference; the medical director adopted Medical Control-directed pediatric eligibility, maximum, rate and preparation for this release on October 31, 2026.

Highlighted UP recommendations accepted by the medical director October 31, 2026 and incorporated into the review build. This is not full-system clinical release; product/device-specific, credentialing and legal/agency validation gates remain where stated.

Medical director revised all adult ketorolac dosing to 15 mg IV once or 30 mg IM once, maximum; no 60 mg IM dose. This applies also to age ≥65 or weight <50 kg and does not establish expanded AEMT authority.

Scoped trauma-review revisions accepted October 30, 2026: expanded AEMT parenteral analgesia is disabled by default until current Tennessee drug/route authority, documented approved training, agency credentialing/competency, and medication-/route-/patient-specific medical-director standing orders are verified. This is not full-system clinical release.
TB-11 express Medical Control authorization remains required for ketamine analgesia in suspected penetrating/open-globe injury.

Medical-director approved adult UP-11 for patients 16 years of age or older and directed provider-specific care: oral acetaminophen/ibuprofen by EMT, AEMT, or Paramedic; IV acetaminophen/ketorolac by Paramedic, with expanded AEMT authority disabled until separately verified for the specified drug, route, and patient group; and opioids/analgesic-dose ketamine by Paramedic only.
Medical-director removed nitrous oxide because it is not on the Claiborne formulary and removed aspirin as an analgesic while retaining aspirin only for its approved cardiac indication.

Medical-director approved acetaminophen 650–1,000 mg PO, ibuprofen 400 mg PO, weight-based acetaminophen infused over 15 minutes once (≥50 kg: 1,000 mg; <50 kg: 15 mg/kg, maximum 750 mg; IV, or IO only with separately verified authorization), and ketorolac 15 mg IV or 30 mg IM once with the medication-specific contraindications documented in UP-11.

Medical-director approved Paramedic opioid limits: fentanyl maximum total 100 mcg, morphine maximum total 10 mg, and hydromorphone maximum total 1 mg; one opioid is selected and different opioids are not combined.

Medical-director approved analgesic ketamine 0.3 mg/kg IV/IO slowly over 10 minutes to maximum 30 mg per dose, repeat every 20 minutes for maximum three doses; or 0.5–1 mg/kg IN once to maximum 100 mg when vascular access is unavailable.
Medical-director directed against routine initial opioid/ketamine combination therapy and required full reassessment before changing agents.

Medical-director required cardiac monitoring for all systemic nonoral analgesia and continuous SpO₂ and waveform EtCO₂ for opioid or ketamine administration, with reassessment at least every 5–10 minutes and at handoff.

Medical-director approved ventilatory support before titrated naloxone for opioid-induced hypoventilation, ondansetron 4 mg for associated nausea, and the documented medication-specific contraindications and safety exclusions.
Medical-director approved PM-04 Pediatric Pain Control as the pediatric pathway for patients age 2 through younger than 16 years; UP-11 is not used for that age group.
UP-11 may be used as Reviewed beta content; final Approved status remains pending completion of the full protocol and formulary reconciliation process.
